Confine the Free Break-Points of a Term Away From the Held Ones

Source: R/seg_pin.R
seg_pin.Rd

Prepares a continuous seg() term for a fit in which some of its coefficients are held at given values. Each break-point whose position is not held stays in the interval between the held positions that surround it, with at least min_obs observations between it and each of them, and the coefficients of a break-point of which a coefficient is held are not exchanged with those of another when the positions cross.

Usage

seg_pin(term, held, start = NULL, min_obs = 2L)

Arguments

term

A built seg() term whose break-point positions carry no development.

held

A named numeric vector of the coefficients of the term that are held. The names are those of term@coef_names. The values of the coefficients that carry the positions of break-points are positions; the other values are not read, and the coefficient of the linear part does not affect the break-points.

start

The positions of the break-points from which the fit starts, one for each break-point, ordered as the term orders them. The default is the positions of the term.

min_obs

The smallest number of observations between a free and a held break-point, a positive integer.

Value

The term, with the intervals of its break-points and the groups within which they exchange labels recorded. seg_limits() returns the intervals.

Details

Two break-points of a continuous term at one position make two columns of the block equal. As the free break-point approaches the held one, the coefficients of the two changes of slope grow without bound in opposite directions, because the pair then imitates a jump of the level. Without this function the relabeling of crossed break-points in term_refresh() exchanges the coefficients of the held break-point with those of the free one, so that the value held for the first is written onto the second and the fit alternates between two states without converging.

A change of slope is estimated from the observations between its break-point and the next one, so that two observations are the least that identifies it, and the interval of a free break-point leaves that many between it and a held one. The interval is the one, among those that the held positions cut out of the confinement interval of the term, that contains the position in start or, when that position leaves fewer observations than that, the nearest interval with room. The side is therefore the one on which the break-point starts, and the break-point cannot cross a held one during the fit. The held positions are clamped to the confinement interval of the term. Free break-points that share an interval exchange their labels when their positions cross, as in an ordinary fit.

The columns of a free break-point at an end of its interval are zero, as they are at the confinement limits of the term, so that the coefficient stays at the end.

See also

seg_limits(), term_refresh(), seg_hold().

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = sort(runif(100, 0, 10)))
b <- term_build(seg(x, npsi = 2, psi = c(3, 7)), d)
p <- seg_pin(b, held = c(seg.psi2 = 5), start = c(3, 7))
seg_limits(p)
#>          lower    upper
#> psi1 0.8356852 4.935413
#> psi2 0.8356852 9.084412
